transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Pinefall CTO), Ethan Cole (Lead ML Eng), Priya Nair (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Console usage analytics focusing on per-route dashboards and the traffic-to-cost mapping. Discussed tagging, data residency, dedicated vs hosted, and an agreed sandbox pilot.

Topics (auto): per-route view, cost breakdown, caching/batching impact, dedicated capacity, KMS/encryption, sandbox POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is Daniel from our infra team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console flow. We got the invite, thank you.
[00:09] Ethan: Yeah hey, Ethan here. We'll probably deep dive on the route tags and how we map traffic to cost.
[00:13] Daniel: Great — i'll focus on the per-route telemetry and the baseline latency / kernel notes. Quick note: if something sounds off in the audio, sorry, the auto transcript chips in weird sometimes.
[00:20] Priya: no worries, let's go.
[00:24] Samira: OK so first slide-ish, real quick context: Pinefall mentioned earlier that you have a handful of app routes that generate most of your inference volume and you want clearer billing attribution and a way to alert on route-level cost spikes. Is that still right?
[00:36] Maya: yup correct. We've got about six routes that are heavy — two chat flows, one rerank, two batch embed pipelines. They live across k8s and a couple cloud functions.
[00:46] Samira: perfect. We'll jump into the console. (screen share) Alright, this is the main usage lens. The left nav lets you pick 'Per-route' and 'Model-level' views.
[00:59] [00:59] Daniel: quick clar — the per-route picks up tags we inject at request time, so as long as your platform sends x-redwood-route header or route tag in the SDK, it will map. If not, we fall back to model endpoints which is less precise.
[01:16] Ethan: ok so we can add the header in our gateway, should be trivial. Does it increase payload latency?
[01:21] Daniel: it's just metadata, negligible. More importantly, the console shows both token-level cost and amortized GPU time so you can see the traffic→cost delta.
[01:32] [01:32] Samira: here's an example: route A is high tokens but low cost because of caching + batching; route B is chat with long context, high mem, so cost per call spikes. You can filter by timeframe or slice by model variant too.
[01:48] Maya: are those cost numbers pre-tax and do they include dedicated reservation amortization if we go dedicated?
[01:54] Daniel: good Q. The displayed unit cost is based on the active billing mode: hosted shows variable per-token price; if you're on Dedicated the console lets you upload reserved-commit cost or we can ingest it from the contract to show effective $/call. So yes, you can toggle between 'raw unit' and 'amortized commit'.
[02:11] Ethan: interesting, so we can see whether larger commit actually lowers the per-route unit.
[02:15] Samira: exactly. Also our Optimize module will give recommendations — for example a heavy batch embed route might be moved to a quantized variant and batched at 128 which reduces GPU time by ~40% per token in some of our profiles.
[02:29] [02:29] Priya: can we see the quantization recommendation per route? Is that the 'Optimize' tab?
[02:34] Daniel: yes you'll get recommended model variants and quant profiles tied to a route. It's a suggestion, we show expected latency impact and a quality delta estimate from our eval harness.
[02:44] Maya: wanted to clarify data residency: some of our data is PII. We're considering VPC/private deploys for those flows. How does per-route mapping work across private deployments?
[02:55] Samira: good question. For Private deployments we support the same telemetry — the agent in your VPC pipes anonymized usage to the control plane; you can also opt to keep metrics in your VPC only. If you pick 'local-only' the console in Redwood-hosted won't show detailed payloads but you'll still get route-level cost aggregates if you opt-in.
[03:13] Ethan: so we'd still be able to compare costs across private vs hosted?
[03:16] Daniel: yes, we can stitch aggregates. The only limitation is debug-level traces which are kept on-prem if you choose.
[03:24] Samira: let me click into a specific route. Here we have timeline of calls, 95th latency, token distribution, and cost breakdown. Notice the shaded area — that's our batch/caching hit rate.
[03:36] [03:36] System/auto: Speaker change unclear
[03:38] Ethan: i see in the chart a sudden spike on Oct 11 — can we attributed that to a model fallback?
[03:42] Daniel: yep, the console correlates errors/fallbacks to cost. In that case, the routing policy failed over to a larger-context model which increased per-call tokens. You can configure automatic rollback or throttles per-route to prevent runaway spend.
[03:54] Maya: who's allowed to change routing policies? We need RBAC.
[03:58] Samira: RBAC is per-team, so you can make it so only ops or platform leads modify production policies. We also maintain immutable audit logs for any policy or model change — good for compliance.
[04:10] Priya: talk to me about KMS — we use AWS KMS for keys, we need to ensure model logs aren't stored in plaintext.
[04:16] Daniel: Redwood integrates with KMS/HSM providers. You can provide a customer-managed key for secrets and at-rest encryption. For private deployments we can also use your HSM. Logs are encrypted and access is controlled through SSO/SCIM, and we surface audit trails in the console.
[04:32] Maya: and SOC2? any gap?
[04:35] Samira: we're SOC2 Type II certified — we'll share the security pack after the call. Daniel: and the pack includes pen-test summary, encryption details, and our SOC2 report redacted.
[04:46] [04:46] Ethan: some nitty gritty — our batch embedding job runs hourly and produces big payloads; can Redwood handle 2k concurrency and 1.2M tokens per minute across routes?
[04:58] Daniel: yes, on Dedicated you'd reserve GPU pools sized for that throughput. Console shows projected tail latency given your QPS and model choices, and you can simulate a load test from the sandbox to validate.
[05:10] Samira: do you have a timeline for starting a POC?
[05:13] Maya: we want to validate before budget cycle — ideally run a 2-week sandbox in early November.
[05:18] Samira: perfect, we can provision a sandbox with dedicated slices for your heavy routes.
[05:22] Daniel: i'll walk through the sandbox topology briefly. (shares diagram) We'll give you a small Dedicated pool and a hosted fallback. The console will show per-route costs with and without caching enabled so you can measure runbook impact.
[05:36] [05:36] System/auto: Possible speaker noise
[05:38] Priya: what's the instrumentation required? We have an API gateway and some serverless fns.
[05:43] Daniel: SDK injection is easiest — set x-redwood-route or use the route param in our Python/Go client. For serverless we have a small middleware snippet. For gateways you can set the header at the ingress.
[05:53] Ethan: if we forget to tag some calls, how bad is it?
[05:57] Daniel: uncovered calls will be bucketed under 'unknown route' and we provide heuristics to retroactively map by modeling IP+path patterns for a best-effort reconciliation. But tagging is the single most reliable approach.
[06:11] Maya: can we export per-route chargebacks to our finance system? CSV/BigQuery?
[06:16] Samira: yes — exports to S3/BigQuery/CSV are available, plus a webhook if you want near-realtime. You can map routes to cost centers and push to your ledger.
[06:26] [06:26] Ethan: on the UI, can we set alert thresholds by percent-of-commit per route?
[06:30] Daniel: yep, there are alert rules — percentage, absolute $ amount, or token anomaly alerts. Alerts can be routed to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.
[06:38] Samira: quick demo of a cost drill. (click) Here we break a spike down by token bucket: model, quantization, and whether the call used long context. See the right column? It shows 'suggested action' — e.g., enable batching or reduce temperature.
[06:53] Maya: reduce temperature for cost? does that effect quality metrics we care about?
[06:58] Daniel: temperature affects generation variance, not token count. The recommended actions are model/infra level: switch to a quantized variant, increase batch size, or add prefix caching to cut repeated tokens. We also surface eval delta so you can weigh quality vs cost.
[07:14] [07:14] Priya: about caching — our chat flow has lots of repeated system prompts, what's Redwood's recommendation?
[07:20] Daniel: prefix caching handles system prompts and repeated context; combined with KV cache it's effective. Console shows cache hit rate and estimated savings if you enable it. For example in one customer we shaved 35% off token spend by caching static system messages.
[07:34] Ethan: do you have sample dashboards we can import?
[07:36] Samira: yes i'll share JSON dashboards and a sample workbook for your finance team.
[07:41] [07:41] System/auto: short pause
[07:44] Maya: curious about model fallbacks — what happens in cross-region outages?
[07:48] Daniel: we have smart routing — you can define routing rules with region preferences. If a region is down, traffic fails over to next best region or model variant. Console shows failover events and cost delta for each failover. We also log the decision tree for auditing.
[08:05] Priya: any gotchas on latency when falling back to a different region?
[08:09] Daniel: yes you'll see increased network latency; console overlays network RTT with token processing time, so you can isolate where latency is introduced.
[08:19] Samira: i'd like to show the POC template: two-week sandbox, supply 6 routes, we instrument tagging, run baseline tests, enable Optimize suggestions, and then we'll produce a final report with cost per route and suggested commit size.
[08:37] Ethan: sounds good, can we get a sample SLA for Dedicated?
[08:40] Samira: absolutely — i'll attach the SLA and the reserved pricing terms.
[08:44] [08:44] System/auto: minor overlap in voices
[08:46] Maya: quick question from finance — if a route is moved to_quantized model, does the credit go to model team or infra? (laughs)
[08:54] Samira: (laugh) it's configurable, the export includes a routing->cost-center map so you decide the accounting.
[08:59] Daniel: also note our chargeback CSV includes columns for model_variant, route_tag, cost_center, and commit_amortized_flag.
[09:09] Priya: about security docs — we'll need the full network diagram for Private deploy.
[09:13] Samira: we'll include that in the security pack.
[09:16] [09:16] System/auto: speaker uncertain
[09:18] Ethan: there was earlier mention of automatic re-routing if cost spikes. Can we set a policy like 'throttle route after $X spike in 1h'?
[09:24] Daniel: yes you can create SLO-based policies that trigger rate limiting or model fallback. They are pluggable into your governance rules and require ops approval depending on RBAC.
[09:34] Maya: let's talk experiment: we want to trial moving our high-volume embedding pipeline to a quantized variant and measure quality. What do we need to provide?
[09:43] Samira: provide a sample of prompt-response pairs and a quality rubric. We'll run the quantized variant on the sandbox and run eval comparisons; Daniel will provide instructions for running microbenchmarks.
[09:54] Daniel: one tip: include a small held-out evaluation set and we'll produce an approximate quality delta and comms-level recommendations.
[10:03] [10:03] System/auto: background noise
[10:05] Priya: how much effort to add team-level RBAC and SSO? We have Okta already.
[10:10] Samira: we support SAML/Okta; integration is turnkey, usually a one-day setup for your identity admin.
[10:16] Maya: does billing data get sent to our own billing bucket? We prefer invoices in our finance flow.
[10:21] Samira: we can push detailed invoices + route-level exports to your S3/BigQuery, and you can fetch cost reports daily.
[10:28] Ethan: any known limits on the console for dashboards? e.g., number of routes, cardinality?
[10:33] Daniel: console handles tens of thousands of routes; large cardinality may need rollup strategies but we support tags, hierarchies, and regex-based grouping.
[10:42] Samira: (walks to the 'compare' view) Here we can compare two time windows side-by-side. For example, enabling caching cut costs by 28% on route C while slightly bumping 95th latency by 20ms. We surface tradeoffs so you can make informed decisions.
[10:56] Maya: can you show the audit trail for a model rollout? We need to see what was changed and by whom.
[11:01] Daniel: sure — clicking into a rollout shows who initiated the canary, the % traffic progression, and the metric deltas. Each step is auditable with a timestamp and user id tied to SCIM user.
[11:12] Priya: is there a way to auto-rollback based on quality regressions?
[11:16] Daniel: yes, you can set automatic rollback thresholds on eval metrics or latency/cost.
[11:21] [11:21] System/auto: overlapping speech
[11:23] Samira: any blockers from Pinefall's side for starting the sandbox early November?
[11:28] Maya: we need security pack, the sandbox access, and engineering time to add headers.
[11:32] Samira: we'll send the pack and sandbox invite today, Daniel will run the baseline on Nov 9 as we discussed.
[11:39] Ethan: timeline noted. Also would like a quick guide for mapping our existing billing tags to Redwood route tags.
[11:45] Samira: i'll include that mapping template.
[11:48] [11:48] System/auto: short pause
[11:50] Maya: final question — any competitors that do a better job on attribution?
[11:55] Daniel: some vendors provide raw metrics but fewer provide both cost amortization and Optimize recommendations at route granularity. We also focus on production runbooks (fallbacks/rollouts) which tends to be the differentiator.
[12:09] Priya: thanks that's helpful.
[12:11] Samira: ok to recap — next steps: we send sandbox + security pack (Samira), Pinefall to send route list and sample payloads (Ethan), Daniel runs latency baseline and shares kernel/quantization recs (Daniel). We'll reconvene after the baseline.
[12:25] Maya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:28] Samira: thank you all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
